text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.

- The University of Zambia has been closed indefinitely, more than 10 students arrested and student leaders expelled following a riot by students opposed to the manner in which the government intends to hold general elections scheduled for November 18.
- Four opposition parties have challenged the nomination of president Frederick Chiluba as a presidential candidate over his citizenship, state radio and television reported.

The Electoral Commission warned on Monday that it may bar some monitor groups from observing the November 18 polls. It was responding to press reports that some Western governments had bribed some monitoring groups to declare the elections not free and fair.

THE POST - President Frederick Chiluba and former president Kenneth Kaunda today meet South African president Nelson Mandela and other regional leaders in South Africa to try to resolve Zambia's electoral crisis, foreign affairs ministry officials said.
